passage: Chetan had borrowed a small sum from a phone app to pay his exam form fee. Cash arrived in minutes. Then the calls began. Threats, rude words, and messages sent to the contacts in his phone, calling him a thief. Every ring made his stomach drop. In a panic he took a second loan from another app to pay the first, and then the second began calling too. He sat on the steps of the bus stand in the kasba, feeling trapped. Leela didi, who worked at the Common Service Centre, saw his face and sat down. He told her everything. "Don't take one loan to pay another," she said. "Take screenshots of every call and message." Together they went to the police station and used the official complaint site. Chetan still felt shaky, but he no longer felt alone.

qa.q: Where did Chetan sit when Leela didi found him?
qa.a: He sat on the steps of the bus stand in the kasba.

qa.q: Why did Chetan take a second loan from another app?
qa.a: He was panicking and felt trapped, and hoped a second loan would stop the calls of the first.

qa.q: What could Chetan do next, besides the complaint?
qa.a: He can stop taking new loans, keep saving screenshots of the calls and messages, and keep his family or another trusted adult informed.

qa.q: How might Leela didi have seen Chetan's situation?
qa.a: Leela didi noticed his face, sat down and listened, so she seems to see a young person in trouble who needs support, not blame.

grounding: An instant loan app floods the protagonist with threats and shaming; he stops borrowing to repay, saves evidence and tells a trusted adult and uses official complaint channels.
